citation: Mirzadeh, Alizadeh, Shahrokhi, Tuzel, Bengio and Farajtabar (2024), GSM-Symbolic: Understanding the Limitations of Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models, ICLR 2025 camera-ready; arXiv 2410.05229 v2 (27 Aug 2025)
text_source: GSM8K grade-school maths word problems (100 seeds)
feature: Accuracy across template instantiations; names-only and numbers-only variants; added or removed clauses; irrelevant clause (NoOp)
method: Symbolic templates with typed slots and validity checks; 50 instances per template; 8-shot CoT; about 25 models from 2B to frontier
outcome: Exact-answer accuracy, its spread across 50 datasets
pit_handling: Fresh instances defeat memorised answers; contamination offered as explanation, not tested
informs_decision: Template-plus-variant generation for S1 reasoning items; numbers-only and NoOp controls; report spread across instantiations; clause count as difficulty axis

citation: Xie, Orel, Thareja and 22 others (2025), FinChain: A Symbolic Benchmark for Verifiable Chain-of-Thought Financial Reasoning, arXiv 2506.02515 v3 (8 Jan 2026)
text_source: Synthetic finance word problems from 290 executable templates (58 topics, 12 domains); 2,900 items
feature: Step-level agreement with a gold step chain; final-answer correctness
method: Python templates emit gold steps; ChainEval = DTW alignment of steps gated by cosine similarity and 5% numeric tolerance; 26 models zero-shot
outcome: ChainEval; final-answer correctness; Spearman with expert process ratings (100 responses)
pit_handling: Claimed contamination-free by regeneration; no held-out templates or contamination test
informs_decision: Generators should emit gold intermediate figures so stated numbers in a model's reasoning can be checked; similarity-based step metrics reach only about 0.6 rank correlation with experts; report answer and step accuracy separately

citation: Shetty, Upadhayaya, Shah, Nayak, Fee and Jagabathula (2025), Advanced Financial Reasoning at Scale: A Comprehensive Evaluation of Large Language Models on CFA Level III, FinLLM@IJCAI 2025; arXiv 2507.02954 v2 (22 Sep 2025) (deep note written by stream 13a: papers/shetty-2025-cfa-level-iii-evaluation.md; the per-model grader gaps were read for this stream)
text_source: Mock CFA Level III exams (paywalled prep provider): 60 MCQ, 43 essays
feature: Essay scores from an LLM grader and one certified human grader
method: GPT-4.1 strict rubric grader, integer scores; human grader on 989 answers; 23 models; zero-shot, CoT self-consistency, Self-Discover
outcome: MCQ accuracy; essay score; LLM-human grade gap and exact agreement
pit_handling: Not tested; paywall argued to reduce contamination
informs_decision: LLM grader 5.6 points harsher on average, 70.4% exact agreement, and its bias varies by graded model from -3.3 to +14.1: validate any S1 judge per evaluated arm; avoid holistic integer scoring

citation: Szymanski, Ziems, Eicher-Miller, Li, Jiang and Metoyer (2024), Limitations of the LLM-as-a-Judge Approach for Evaluating LLM Outputs in Expert Knowledge Tasks, arXiv 2410.20266 v1
text_source: 25 expert-knowledge instructions in dietetics and mental health, paired responses
feature: Pairwise preference agreement of a GPT-4 judge with 10 experts and 10 lay users per domain
method: AlpacaEval-style pairwise judging, general and expert-persona prompts; overall and aspect questions
informs_decision: Judge-expert 60-68% against expert-expert 72-75%; judge aligns with lay users (76-80%) and rewards length; persona no fix: do not use preference judging for S1 reasoning items

citation: Chandak, Goel, Prabhu, Hardt and Geiping (2025), Answer Matching Outperforms Multiple Choice for Language Model Evaluation, arXiv 2507.02856 v1
text_source: MATH, MMLU-Pro and GPQA-Diamond (filtered for unique answers)
feature: Agreement of grading methods with human grades
method: Choice-only shortcut test; free-form answers matched to a reference by a small or large LM; Scott's pi
outcome: Scott's pi against humans or MATH-Verify; rankings; cost
informs_decision: Give reasoning items a unique short answer and grade by rule or reference matching; small matchers reach human-level agreement; reference-free judges err leniently; test a choice-only baseline before any MCQ

citation: Paleka, Pallavi Sudhir, Alvarez, Bhat, Shen, Wang and Tramèr (2024), Consistency Checks for Language Model Forecasters, submitted to ICLR 2025; arXiv 2412.18544 v2
text_source: Metaculus/Manifold and news-generated binary questions resolving 2024; synthetic 2028 questions
feature: Violation of logical consistency across related forecasts (arbitrage and frequentist metrics)
method: LLM-generated question tuples for 10 checks; correlation with Brier score across forecasters; consistency-enforcing wrapper
outcome: Violation rate; correlation with Brier score
pit_handling: Questions resolve after cutoffs; consistency needs no resolution
informs_decision: Consistency across related S1 questions is a cheap gold-free diagnostic (conditional checks track accuracy, r up to 0.92; negation unstable) but not a target: enforcing it did not improve accuracy

citation: Koijen and Levy (2026), Assessing the Benefits of Optimized Agentic AI Systems for Asset Pricing, NBER WP 35431 / BFI WP 2026-100 (July 2026)
text_source: Earnings-call transcripts and consensus EPS, 1,849 US announcements, Q4 2025
feature: LLM scalar prediction of the announcement return from transcript (full or summarised); optimised prompts and rule books
method: Real-time protocol with frozen prompts; cross-sectional regression on percentile-ranked abnormal returns; GEPA and ACE optimisation on first half of quarter
pit_handling: All events after model cutoffs; prompts frozen before each event; no web access; optimisation on earlier events only
informs_decision: Prospective outcome label for release understanding: market reaction scored against the surprise; best R-squared 14-17%, so underpowered for small S1 test sets; rule book from a large model transfers to small ones

citation: Arora, Wei, Hicks and 9 others (2025), HealthBench: Evaluating Large Language Models Towards Improved Human Health, arXiv 2505.08775 v1
text_source: 5,000 health conversations; 48,562 physician-written criteria
feature: Score from item-specific signed binary criteria graded one at a time by GPT-4.1
method: Rubric criteria with -10 to +10 points; grader meta-evaluated on 34 consensus criteria against physicians by macro F1
informs_decision: Template for open-ended S1 items: many binary, signed, item-specific criteria (generable from gold figures); validate grader against human-human ceiling (55-75%); small graders worse (nano 0.58 against 0.71)

citation: Wu, Qiu, Ross, Akyürek, Chen, Wang, Kim, Andreas and Kim (2024), Reasoning or Reciting? Exploring the Capabilities and Limitations of Language Models Through Counterfactual Tasks, NAACL 2024; arXiv 2307.02477 v3 (abstract read)
text_source: 11 tasks with default and counterfactual rule variants
method: Counterfactual task variants that change default assumptions
informs_decision: Above-chance but consistently lower accuracy on counterfactual variants: supports counterfactual-rule items (for example an unusual but stated accounting convention) to separate procedure from recall

citation: Srivastava, M B, P V, Menon, Sukumar, T, Philipose, Prince and Thomas (2024), Functional Benchmarks for Robust Evaluation of Reasoning Performance, and the Reasoning Gap, arXiv 2402.19450 v1 (abstract read)
text_source: MATH rewritten as functional variants (MATH())
method: Template-generated functional snapshots; reasoning gap = relative static minus functional accuracy
informs_decision: Gaps of 58% to 80% for strong models: release new snapshots of S1 templates per evaluation and report a static-functional gap

citation: Zheng, Chiang, Sheng and 10 others (2023), Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena, NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks; arXiv 2306.05685 v4 (abstract read)
text_source: MT-bench questions; Chatbot Arena conversations
method: GPT-4 as pairwise and single-answer judge; bias analysis (position, verbosity, self-enhancement)
outcome: Agreement with expert and crowd preferences
informs_decision: Over 80% agreement on general chat equals human-human; this is the optimistic baseline that expert-domain studies do not reproduce

citation: Wang, Li, Chen, Cai, Zhu, Lin, Cao, Liu, Liu and Sui (2023), Large Language Models are not Fair Evaluators, arXiv 2305.17926 v2 (abstract read)
text_source: Vicuna benchmark questions
method: Swap response order; multiple-evidence, balanced-position and human-in-the-loop calibration
outcome: Win rates; agreement with human labels
informs_decision: Order alone flipped a comparison (Vicuna-13B beat ChatGPT on 66 of 80 queries with ChatGPT judging): any pairwise grading in S1 must balance positions

citation: Min, Krishna, Lyu, Lewis, Yih, Koh, Iyyer, Zettlemoyer and Hajishirzi (2023), FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation, EMNLP 2023; arXiv 2305.14251 v2 (abstract read)
text_source: Biographies generated by 13 LMs
method: Decompose output into atomic facts; check each against a knowledge source; automated estimator
informs_decision: Claim-level verification with automated error under 2%: for S1 open answers, split into numeric and directional claims and check each against the gold figures

citation: Zheng, Zhang, Zhang, Lin, Lu, Yu, Liu, Zhou and Lin (2025), ProcessBench: Identifying Process Errors in Mathematical Reasoning, ACL 2025; arXiv 2412.06559 v4 (abstract read)
text_source: 3,400 competition maths solutions with expert-marked first error
method: Models identify the earliest wrong step; PRMs against prompted critics
informs_decision: Existing process reward models fail beyond GSM8K/MATH; prompted critics do better: for S1 prefer rule checks of stated figures over learned step verifiers

citation: Lightman, Kosaraju, Burda, Edwards, Baker, Lee, Leike, Schulman, Sutskever and Cobbe (2023), Let's Verify Step by Step, arXiv 2305.20050 v1 (abstract read)
text_source: MATH problems; 800,000 step-level human labels (PRM800K)
method: Process against outcome supervision of reward models
outcome: Problems solved with best-of-N under each reward model
informs_decision: Process supervision beats outcome supervision (78% of a MATH subset): step labels have value, and S1 templates can provide them for free

citation: Matlin, Theerthala, Gupta, JM, Castilla, Ng and Chava (2026), FinForge: Semi-Synthetic Financial Benchmark Generation, arXiv 2601.06747 v2 (abstract read)
text_source: 100,000 curated finance documents (143M tokens); 5,000+ QA pairs
method: Expert-guided corpus; Gemini 2.5 Flash generates and validates questions; human validation
informs_decision: LLM-generated finance QA at scale with human validation; leading models near 80%; precedent for semi-synthetic generation, not for rule gold

citation: Larsen, Laurent, Rakhmasari, Turgut and Antulov-Fantulin (2026), V-FiLLM: Verified Financial LLM Reasoning Benchmark, arXiv 2608.11047 v1 (abstract and Section 4 read)
text_source: Synthetic 10-Q-style and simplified spreadsheets of synthetic companies
method: Executable computation trees over table cells; difficulty by depth, breadth, scale; perturbations of question-irrelevant cells
informs_decision: Gold by construction; accuracy falls up to 51% with depth and up to 47 points when irrelevant cells are corrupted; unit or scale shifts most damaging (Gemma-31B 98.4 to 3.0): invariance controls for S1

citation: Haque, Papadimitriou, Mensah, Ma, Guo, Sain, Kaur, Smiley and Liu (2026), Deep FinResearch Bench: Evaluating AI's Ability to Conduct Professional Financial Investment Research, arXiv 2604.21006 v1 (abstract read)
text_source: Investment research reports from deep-research agents and professionals
method: Three scoring dimensions: qualitative rigour, forecasting and valuation accuracy, claim verifiability; automated scoring
informs_decision: Precedent for scoring analysis partly by verifiable claims and partly by forecast accuracy; no agreement numbers in abstract

citation: Zhu, Jiang, Xu, Yao, Cheng, Ding and Xu (2026), FinReasoning: A Hierarchical Benchmark for Reliable Financial Research Reporting, arXiv 2603.19254 v2 (abstract read)
text_source: Chinese financial research reporting tasks
method: Separate scores for semantic consistency, data alignment and deep insight; hallucination correction; 12-indicator rubric
informs_decision: Supports scoring data alignment separately from insight; finance-tuned Fin-R1 gives moderate insight but weak auditing

citation: Jin, Li, Zhang and Yan (2026), FinRpt: Dataset, Evaluation System and LLM-based Multi-agent Framework for Equity Research Report Generation, AAAI 2026; arXiv 2511.07322 v3 (abstract read)
text_source: Automatically built equity research report dataset from 7 financial data types
method: 11-metric evaluation system; multi-agent generator trained with SFT and RL
informs_decision: Report-generation evaluation exists but with no human agreement figures in the abstract; weak evidence for grading open analysis

citation: Karger, Bastani, Chen, Jacobs, Halawi, Zhang and Tetlock (2024), ForecastBench: A Dynamic Benchmark of AI Forecasting Capabilities, arXiv 2409.19839 v5 (abstract read)
text_source: 1,000 automatically generated forecasting questions, regularly updated
method: Questions about events unresolved at submission; human expert, public and LLM forecasts on 200
informs_decision: Dynamic, unresolved-at-submission questions are the general form of S1's prospective outcome items; experts beat the best LLM (p < 0.001)

citation: Patel, Chen, He, Wang, Li, Xiao and Liu (2025), Reasoning Models Ace the CFA Exams, arXiv 2512.08270 v1 (abstract read)
text_source: 980 mock CFA questions, Levels I to III
method: Reasoning models on MCQ and constructed responses
informs_decision: Frontier reasoning models score 86-98% on CFA-style material: exam-style finance is saturated and contaminated, so S1 reasoning needs new release-based items

citation: Arcuschin, Janiak, Krzyzanowski, Rajamanoharan, Nanda and Conmy (2026), Chain-of-Thought Reasoning In The Wild Is Not Always Faithful, ICML 2026; arXiv 2503.08679 v6 (abstract read)
text_source: Paired comparative questions (is X bigger than Y; is Y bigger than X)
method: Ask both orderings; detect contradictory answers each with a plausible rationale
informs_decision: Reversed-pair questions detect rationalised reasoning cheaply (up to 13% in production models, 0.04-0.37% in frontier reasoning models): add mirrored comparison pairs to S1

citation: Sunkavalli (2026), LLM Judges as Raters: A Pre-Registered Audit of Severity, Halo, Reliability, and Version Instability in LLM Essay Scoring on Public Corpora, arXiv 2608.29517 v1 (abstract read)
text_source: 2,377 essays from two public corpora; 12 judges from 4 providers
method: Pre-registered rater-effects analysis: severity, halo, reliability, version contrasts
outcome: Judge-human correlation; severity spread; version shifts
informs_decision: Judge-human correlations .47-.56; severity spread far above human raters; every version change shifted severity: pin judge version and re-validate after any change

citation: Shu, Liu, Zhang and Du (2025), FinCall-Surprise: A Large Scale Multi-modal Benchmark for Earning Surprise Prediction, arXiv 2510.03965 v1 (abstract read)
text_source: 2,688 earnings calls 2019-2021 with transcripts, audio and slides
method: 26 LLMs predict earnings surprise
pit_handling: Not addressed in abstract; data predate current model cutoffs
informs_decision: Outcome label on pre-cutoff calls with class imbalance that makes accuracy misleading: use balanced metrics and post-cutoff data
